MakerSquare is Austin's school of applied AI: in-person builder programs for
non-technical professionals — a 2-week immersive cohort, 3-day weekend
workshops, and private team training. Students ship a live website, a working
AI agent, and an automated workflow, then present at Demo Day.

Contact: hello@makersquare.ai · https://www.makersquare.ai/

The shift

### The wall just came down.

For fifty years, building software meant being a developer. That wall is gone — like the Berlin Wall came down, the barrier between having an idea and shipping it just fell. If you can describe what you want, you can build it, and automate almost anything you do in a day. No CS degree. No engineering team. Your expertise and the right tools are enough now.

Two of our August graduates — and the working tools they walked out with, running on their own jobs.

Chris Cox

Director of System Performance · Hesed House (homeless shelter)

What he built

An ops dashboard plus two agents for the shelter — one that scouts grant and funding opportunities, one that finds voucher-friendly housing for guests — each dropping a weekly digest in his inbox, so staff stop hunting ten sites by hand.

> “The biggest win isn’t what I built — it’s what I can do going forward. There’s nothing they could hand me that I couldn’t build a solution for.”

![Jennifer Francis](images/cohort2/avatar-jennifer.jpg?v=1)
Jennifer Francis

Construction & Facilities Project Management

What she built

An agent that handles every incoming RFI and submittal email — reads it, downloads the file, files and renames it to spec, and logs it to the right project hub. Four manual steps on every email, gone.

> “I could take a real-world problem, build a solution for it, and do it in two weeks — something that felt unfathomable before.”

Who it's for

### We don't teach engineers. We teach people who know their field.

Operators & business owners

#### Half your week is repeatable. Build the AI that does it.

Proposals, reports, follow-ups, invoicing — you already know which parts of your business should run themselves. Knowing what to automate is the hard part. Building it is now learnable.

Professionals & career builders

#### Domain expertise plus AI is the rarest profile in your field.

Marketing, finance, healthcare, law — every industry is short on people who understand the work and can also build with AI. That combination is the career moat.

Founders & first-time builders

#### Stop waiting for a technical co-founder.

If you can describe the product clearly, you can ship the first version yourself. The idea and the market knowledge were always the scarce part.

Not the right fit if…

— You're after a certificate, not working tools
— You want self-paced videos, not a room full of builders
— Two full weeks in Austin isn't possible right now
— You'd rather study the theory than ship

Who it's for

### You don't need a technical background. You need to know your field.

Operators & business owners

#### You run something. AI should be doing half of it.

Reports, proposals, client emails, internal workflows. You know what needs automating. We help you build it.

Professionals & career builders

#### Your expertise is the advantage. Add the AI layer.

Years in marketing, finance, healthcare, law. That domain knowledge is the moat. We teach the technical layer on top of it.

Founders & first-time builders

#### You have the idea. Skip the technical co-founder.

A clear problem, a real market, the drive to ship. MakerSquare is the fastest path from idea to working product.

Not the right fit if…

— You want a certificate without building anything real
— You're looking for a self-paced online course
— You can't commit two full weeks in Austin
— You want to learn theory before you're ready to ship something

Why full immersion

### Not a certificate course. An actual transformation.

We get it — 2 weeks is a real commitment. Here's why the immersion pays for itself, and why it's less disruptive than it sounds.

#### Depth a course can't give you.

Most "AI programs" are webinars with homework. You leave with buzzwords and nothing working. Real skill is layered — each day builds on the last. Two weeks of full focus is what turns "I've heard of Claude" into "I just shipped this."

The 2 weeks makes you the person who builds — three shipped products, and the skill to keep going.

#### You're not taking 2 weeks off work.

Every project you build at MakerSquare is your actual work. Real clients, real problems, real workflows — just solved with AI. You leave with delivered solutions, not fake portfolio pieces.

The program runs 9–3. Afternoons are yours if anything urgent comes up. Come back in two weeks knowing how to work twice as fast. You haven't fallen behind — you've leapt ahead.

> “You can watch someone put up a slideshow anywhere. But if you want somebody to sit right next to you and work on your problem, at your computer — that’s where the value is.”

"Most people say they can't do 2 weeks. Most of them, once they see the outcomes, find a way. The ones who don't aren't who this is for. "

Questions

### Things people usually ask us.

Do I need to know how to code? No. Basic computer fluency and real experience in your field. That's it. We've had doctors, lawyers, real estate agents, and marketing directors build exceptional AI products.

What's the time commitment? Mon-Fri, 9am to 3pm for 2 weeks (30 hrs/week in class), plus optional Saturday office hours.

Why does this have to be 2 weeks? Can't I learn at my own pace? No — and that's intentional. AI skills compound on each other. Day 4 builds on Day 3. Space it out and you're relearning basics every week instead of pushing forward. Online AI courses have a 95% dropout rate because there's no consequence for skipping. Two weeks in a room with 14 other serious people means you show up, you build, and you leave with something real. The people who find a way to make 2 weeks work are exactly the people who get the most out of it.

How selective is it? small cohorts. First-come, first-served — pay full tuition via Stripe. We ask a few questions to make sure you get the most out of the two weeks.

What do I actually walk away with? A live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — all deployed — live on the internet, not exercises. A 5-minute demo you delivered on stage to Austin's tech community. A cohort of operators who become your long-term network. And a skill set you own for life. If you complete the program and don't have everything you build deployed, we refund you in full.

What does $3,999 include? 2 weeks in-person instruction, 24-hour async support, optional Saturday office hours, Demo Day, guest speakers, alumni network. Not included: ~$15–30 in AI service fees and housing (details shared after enrollment).

I'm coming from out of town. Is that okay? Absolutely. Austin has plenty of short-term rental options near campus. Housing details are shared after enrollment.

Can my employer pay? Yes. We issue invoices and can provide a proposal letter for your employer. Many alumni have their company cover it as professional development.

# AI Bootcamp Curriculum | Learn AI in Austin TX | MakerSquare

> Hands-on AI curriculum: Claude Code, Supabase, voice AI. Ship a website, an agent, and an automated workflow in 2 weeks. For non-technical professionals.

Full Curriculum

## We start where courses end.

No beginner hand-holding. Two weeks, Monday to Friday, 9am to 3pm. Production tools including Claude Code, GitHub, Vercel, Supabase, Composio, Playwright, and more. Updated before every cohort.

1

✓

2

●

3

4

Site, agent & workflow shipped

Before Day 1

### Four tasks. About an hour.

The rule is gather, don't build — so Day 1 starts at full speed.

01

#### Set up your accounts

Claude, GitHub, Vercel, Supabase, Warp, and the Anthropic Console (with $10 in API credits). We send exact links.

02

#### Have your first expert conversation

Talk to Claude about your field like an expert would. Save the conversation — you'll use it on Day 1.

03

#### Know your problem

Four short written answers: what the problem is, who it affects, what inputs it needs, and what "solved" looks like. This is also our fit check.

04

#### Bring your Materials Kit

A real dataset, a few documents, and a list of about 10 real inputs (redacted). Every hands-on day runs on your own material, not toy data.

2 Weeks, 10 Days

### Day by day. Product by product.

1

Week 1: Build

#### Set up the tools. Ship Product 1 by Friday.

Mon

Models + Expert Prompting

Claude

How LLMs actually work. The real differences between Claude, GPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek. Talking to Claude like an expert, not a search engine.

Tue

Your Stack + PRD

Warp GitHub

Warp Terminal, first GitHub push. Draft your capstone PRD with Claude. Scope before you build.

Wed

Website + Deploy

Claude Code Vercel

Build a real landing page in plain English. Connect GitHub to Vercel. Push to main, auto-deploy in 30 seconds. Live URL by end of day.

Thu

Supabase + Claude Skills

Supabase Claude Skills MCP

Databases without jargon. Table, form, dashboard, all wired together. Build your first Claude Skill. Learn how AI connects to your tools.

Fri

Product 1 Ships + Content

Live demo LinkedIn

4-minute live demo to your cohort on real data. Then set up a content habit with Claude. The proof-of-work that gets clients and jobs.

Product 1 live at a public URL

Website + Supabase + Claude Skill, all wired together, shipped Friday

2

Week 2: Automate + Ship

#### Build a real AI agent. Demo Day Friday.

Mon

AI Agents + Automation

Composio Gmail Slack

Pipelines vs. agents. Connect Claude to Gmail, Slack, HubSpot, and 200+ tools via Composio — no integration code. Build automations that run on your real data.

Tue

Browser Control + Voice AI

Playwright Whisper ElevenLabs

Playwright for sites with no API: navigate, extract, schedule. Voice stack: Whisper transcribes, Claude reasons, ElevenLabs speaks.

Wed

Build Your AI Agent · Product 2 Ships

Claude Code Render

Claude Code as a full project collaborator in Warp. Ship a working AI agent that connects to an external tool. Deployed on Render, running on your own data.

Thu

Evals + Data Safety + Capstone Sprint

Evals

Learn to test and trust your AI — evals, document Q&A, and handling data and access safely. Full capstone build, deployed by 2:30pm.

Fri

DEMO DAY

Public event 5 min

Austin tech community in the room. 5 minutes each. Live demo on real data, hard questions, real feedback from builders and investors.

Product 2 ships Wednesday

A working AI agent or automation, deployed and running on your real data

Capstone presented at Demo Day

On stage. Austin's tech community in the room.

Week 1: Foundations

#### Set up the tools. Leave with a PRD.

FAQ

### Questions people ask before booking.

Why should I do this now and not wait? Because the gap between people who can use AI and people who can’t is widening every month — not every year. The ops manager or founder who learns this in September has a head start on everyone who waits until next year. Also: early bird pricing closes Aug 21 for the AI Agent workshop. Same seats, same instructor — $200 more after that.

Which AI workshops are running in Austin in fall 2026? Three 3-day intensives in downtown Austin (Capital Factory / Station Austin, 701 Brazos St): **Build Your First AI Agent** Sep 11–13, **Automate Your Ops with AI** Oct 16–18, and **Build Your First App with AI** Nov 6–8. All Fri–Sun, 9am–4pm. Early bird $999, regular $1,199.

Do I need a technical background? No. If you can use a spreadsheet, you can build in these workshops. These aren’t for engineers — they’re for people who know their domain and want AI working for them in it.

How is this different from online courses or YouTube? You’re building with your actual data, your actual tools, your actual problem — not a made-up exercise. And when you get stuck, a real instructor unblocks you in real time. Online courses have a 95% dropout rate because there’s no consequence for skipping and no one there when it breaks. We fix both of those things.

How is this different from the MakerSquare 2-week program? The 2-week program is a deep immersive — you build 3 full AI products, go from zero to shipping real software, and present on Demo Day. Workshops are focused skill sprints: 3 days, one problem, something running when you leave. Many workshop attendees go on to enroll in the full program. Workshop alumni get $200 off with code WORKSHOP200.

What if I can’t commit to 3 full days? Each day builds on the last — missing one means missing foundational work. If 3 consecutive days is a stretch, the private team format lets you break it into a custom schedule. But honestly: if you can’t find 3 days to invest in your own skills, that’s part of the problem we’re solving. AI gives you those hours back.

Can my company pay by invoice? Yes. Email [hello@makersquare.ai](mailto:hello@makersquare.ai) and we’ll send a proposal and invoice within 24 hours. PO-based payment is supported.

What’s the refund policy? Full refund up to 14 days before the workshop start date. 50% refund up to 48 hours before. No refund after the workshop begins.

Is this a vibe coding bootcamp? The November workshop is, in the sense people usually mean it — you describe what you want and an AI writes the code. The difference from most vibe coding you have seen is that you leave with the app actually deployed at a real URL, on a real database, using the tools engineers use: Claude Code, Supabase and Vercel. Three days, no coding background required. It is a workshop rather than a bootcamp: 3 days, not weeks. If you want the longer version, that is the [2-week program](/immersive).

Want to go deeper?

The **2-week MakerSquare program** is the full build — 3 complete AI products, shipped and presented at a public Demo Day in Austin. Workshop alumni get **$200 off** with code **WORKSHOP200**.

[See the 2-week program](/curriculum)

Rhythm

#### It sticks

The weekly and quarterly cadence that keeps AI adopted and compounding long after we’re gone.

The program

### Learn. Build. Ship. No fluff.

Full days, Mon-Fri. On-site at your office or in Austin. Length is scoped to your program during discovery.

Phase 1 · Learn

#### How AI works. Applied to your work.

- How AI models work (the intuition, not the math)

- Prompt engineering for real business tasks

- AI applied to your team's actual daily work

- Identify automation opportunities across the org

- Scope the project your team will build in Phase 2

End of Phase 1: Every participant has integrated AI into their actual job. Project scope approved by leadership.

Phase 2 · Build

#### Build it. Ship it. Present it.

- Full build sprint on the scoped project

- No-code and low-code AI tools

- Connect to your real data and systems

- Test, refine, document for maintenance

- Present the deployed tool to leadership

End of Phase 2: A deployed, working AI tool. Presented live to leadership. Ready to use from day one.

Outcomes

### Specific outcomes. Not vague skills.

#### One deployed AI tool

Built for your specific workflows and data. Yours to use, modify, and expand. Not a prototype. Something that runs in production when the program ends.

#### A team that knows how to use AI

Not just the one person who was already into it. Every participant leaves knowing how to apply AI to their job and what to automate next.

#### A roadmap of what to build next

Your team identifies 5-10 additional automation opportunities. You know exactly where to invest next, without needing external help.

How it works

### From first call to deployed tool.

Most engagements go from first conversation to Day 1 in under 3 weeks.

01

#### Discovery Call

We talk to you and 1-2 people who know the operations well. We identify the highest-ROI automation opportunity. No long sales cycle.

45 minutes

02

#### Pre-Work Scoping

We work with your team to understand your tools, data sources, and exactly what the project will be. Leadership signs off on scope before anything is built.

2-3 days, on-site or remote

03

#### The Program

Full days on-site. Final day: your team presents a live tool to leadership. We leave documentation, a maintenance guide, and a prioritized roadmap.

Full days, Mon-Fri · Length set during scoping

FAQ

### Questions we hear often.

Do our people need any technical background? No. The only requirement is that participants know your business well. We've run this with lawyers, account managers, operations coordinators, recruiters, and finance teams. People who use computers every day but have never written code. Domain knowledge is the asset. We provide the technical layer.

Can you run this at our office? Yes. On-site delivery is available for teams of 12 or more. It's often the right call because it's less disruptive to operations and keeps people in the context of your actual business. Travel and logistics are included in the engagement cost.

Who owns what gets built? You do. 100%. Everything built during the program belongs to your company: the tool, the code, the documentation. We retain no rights. The only thing we ask is permission to describe the engagement category anonymously when talking to prospective clients.

Can you customize the program for a specific team — like sales or marketing? Yes — that's the default, not an exception. A sales team's problems are different from a marketing team's problems, and the curriculum reflects that. During the discovery and scoping phase, we identify which workflows to target, which tools make sense, and what the team will build. The length is also flexible: two weeks is standard, but we can scope something shorter for a focused sprint or longer if there's more to build. The goal is to solve your specific problem, not run a generic AI course.

What if we want to roll this out to the whole company? We run sequential cohorts — one team at a time, each with its own scoping and its own project. Sales builds a sales tool. Marketing builds a marketing tool. Each cohort is customized to that function. For 50+ people, we design a full rollout plan (sequence, timeline, pricing) in the first conversation. Most multi-team engagements are structured so early cohorts build internal momentum for the ones that follow.

How much does corporate AI training cost? Private team workshops and custom programs are quoted per engagement — the price depends on team size, length, and how custom the build is. You get a written proposal within 24 hours of the first call, and there’s no committee process on our side. Individual seats in the public cohort are $3,999.

How long does the training take? The entry format is a private 3-day workshop — your team leaves with working automation on day three. Custom programs are scoped to your goals: length, content, and format are designed around your workflows. Individuals can also join the 2-week public intensive in Austin.

Why train our team instead of hiring an AI consultant? Sometimes a consultant IS the right call — for one deep, specialized system nobody internal will touch. But when the opportunities are spread across sales, ops, and admin, training wins: the capability stays in your people and compounds instead of leaving with the vendor. We wrote an honest comparison: [train your team vs. hire a consultant →](/ai-training-vs-consultants)

How do you handle proprietary data? We work within your security requirements. We can operate entirely on your infrastructure, use only AI tools with no data retention policies, or follow whatever data handling requirements your legal and IT teams specify. We address this explicitly during scoping before any agreement is signed.

Get started

### Tell us about your team.

We respond within one business day. If it sounds like a fit, we schedule a 45-minute discovery call. No pitch deck, no demo. Just a conversation about where AI could make the biggest difference for your team right now.

Prefer to talk it through now? Book a 15-minute call →

FAQ

### Common questions about enrolling.

Do I need a technical background? No. We've had doctors, lawyers, real estate agents, and marketing directors build exceptional AI products. Domain expertise matters more than technical skills.

Why does this have to be 2 weeks? Can't I learn at my own pace? No — and that's intentional. AI skills compound on each other. Day 4 builds on Day 3. Space it out and you're relearning basics every week instead of pushing forward. Online AI courses have a 95% dropout rate because there's no consequence for skipping. Two weeks in a room with 14 other serious people means you show up, you build, and you leave with something real. The people who find a way to make 2 weeks work are exactly the people who get the most out of it.

# FAQ | MakerSquare AI Bootcamp in Austin, TX

> Every question about MakerSquare answered: cost, curriculum, schedule, Demo Day, refunds, and housing. 2-week in-person AI bootcamp in Austin, TX.

Frequently Asked Questions

## Every question about MakerSquare, answered.

Can't find what you're looking for? Email us at [hello@makersquare.ai](mailto:hello@makersquare.ai) — we reply same day.

About the program
Prerequisites
Cost & payment
Curriculum
Logistics
After the program

About the program

#### What is MakerSquare?

MakerSquare is Austin’s school of applied AI for non-technical professionals. The core program is a 2-week in-person builder intensive; we also run private AI training for company teams. Operators, founders, and managers learn to build and deploy real AI products — no coding background required. Students ship a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — deployed and present at a public Demo Day in front of Austin's tech community. [Learn more →](/)

#### What makes MakerSquare different from online AI courses?

MakerSquare is the only multi-week in-person AI builder program currently available. Online courses teach concepts; MakerSquare graduates ship a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — deployed. The in-person, immersive format — 9am to 3pm, Monday through Friday for 2 weeks — means you actually build rather than just watch videos. You also leave with a cohort network and a public Demo Day presentation that online courses can't replicate.

#### When does the next cohort start?

Cohort 2 starts August 3, 2026. MakerSquare runs 4 cohorts in 2026, from July through December. [See the full schedule →](/enroll)

#### How many people are in each cohort?

small cohorts. This is intentional — small enough for real instructor attention and fast feedback on your build, large enough for a meaningful cohort dynamic and network.

#### Does MakerSquare offer corporate training?

Yes — and it’s a core offering. Private 3-day team workshops and fully custom programs for teams of 3 to 15, on-site at your company or in Austin. Your team builds real AI tools for your actual business problems — not generic exercises. Custom pricing. [See corporate training →](/corporate)

Prerequisites & eligibility

#### Do I need to know how to code?

No. MakerSquare is designed specifically for professionals without a technical background. We've had doctors, lawyers, marketers, real estate agents, and finance professionals all build exceptional AI products. Your domain expertise — knowing your industry's problems deeply — is more valuable than coding knowledge.

#### What background do I actually need?

Basic computer fluency (you're comfortable with Google Docs, email, modern software) and real-world domain expertise in your field. Ideally you have a problem in your industry that AI could help solve — that context makes your builds dramatically better. No coding, no math, no computer science required.

#### Is MakerSquare only for people in Austin?

No. MakerSquare welcomes builders from anywhere in the US and internationally. The program runs in person in Austin, TX, so you'll need to be in Austin for the 2 weeks. Austin has a lot of short-term rental options — housing details are shared after enrollment.

#### I'm a recent college grad. Is this right for me?

Yes, if you have a clear problem you want to solve with AI. MakerSquare works best for people who bring real-world context to their builds — a domain you know, a problem worth solving. College grads who've worked in a field, interned in an industry, or have a startup idea they want to build have done well. The program is not a job placement bootcamp — it's a builder program focused on shipping real products.

#### Is there an admissions process?

No interview, no essay, no technical test. You fill out the enrollment form, pay full tuition via Stripe, and your seat is confirmed within 24 hours. Enrollment is open — we trust you know whether this is the right fit for you.

Cost & payment

#### How much does MakerSquare cost?

Tuition is $3,999, paid in full at enrollment via Stripe. A $500 scholarship is available for military veterans, first responders, and educators — reducing tuition to $3,499. [See full pricing →](/immersive)

#### What does tuition include?

Everything in the program: 10 days of instruction (9am–3pm), 24-hour async instructor support during the 2 weeks, a pre-cohort AI toolkit, Demo Day participation, and lifetime access to the MakerSquare alumni Slack. Not included: housing, and approximately $15–30 in AI service fees (Claude, Whisper, ElevenLabs) paid separately during the program.

#### Is there a refund policy?

Yes. Full tuition is paid at enrollment via Stripe. A full refund is available up to 14 days before your cohort start date.

#### What is the refund policy?

Full refund up to 14 days before your cohort start date. 50% refund up to the first day of the program. No refund after the program begins. If MakerSquare cancels a cohort for any reason, you receive a full refund. The guarantee: if you complete the program and don't leave with a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — deployed, you receive a full refund.

#### Can my employer pay for MakerSquare?

Yes. Many participants have their employer cover tuition as professional development. MakerSquare can issue an invoice directly to your company. The scholarship for military, educators, and first responders is also stackable with employer reimbursement — your employer pays the discounted rate, not the original.

#### Is there a scholarship?

Yes. A $500 Service Scholarship is available for military veterans, active duty service members, first responders, and educators. Tuition drops from $3,999 to $3,499. Simple verification process — submit a short form, we verify within 2 business days. [Apply for the scholarship →](/scholarship)

#### Are there any additional fees beyond tuition?

Yes, two things outside of tuition: (1) approximately $15–30 in AI service fees during the program — Claude, Whisper, and ElevenLabs API usage — paid directly to those services; (2) housing if you're coming from out of town, which runs approximately $1,600/month with partner discounts. No income share agreements, no hidden fees.

Curriculum & what you build

#### What is the daily schedule?

Monday through Friday, 9am to 3pm in Austin for 2 weeks (10 teaching days). Optional Saturday office hours from 10am to 1pm for extra build time. Instructors are also available async outside class hours. Pre-work takes 2–3 hours and should be completed before the program starts.

#### What do I actually build?

A live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — all deployed:

**Product 1 (end of Week 1):** A live website with a Claude Skill, deployed to a public URL using Claude Code, Vercel, and Supabase.

**Product 2 (Day 9):** An agentic automation — combining Composio, Playwright browser control, or voice AI with Whisper and ElevenLabs — connected to your real data.

**Capstone (Demo Day):** Your most ambitious product, combining Claude Code, agentic APIs, and the full stack. Presented live on stage at Demo Day. [See full curriculum →](/curriculum)

#### What tools will I learn?

Claude, Claude Code, Warp Terminal, GitHub, Vercel, Render, Supabase, Composio, Playwright, ElevenLabs, and Whisper. No visual automation toys like Zapier or Make — production-level skills only.

#### Why 2 weeks in person? Can't I learn at my own pace?

Real AI skill is layered — each day builds on the last. Doing a little on evenings and weekends means you never hit the depth where it actually clicks. Most "AI courses" are pre-recorded videos and slide decks — you leave with notes, not working tools. Two weeks of full focus is what turns "I've heard of Claude" into "I just shipped this."

The other thing people worry about is losing 2 weeks of work. But every project you build at MakerSquare is your actual work — real clients, real problems, real workflows. You leave with delivered solutions, not fake portfolio pieces. The program runs 9–3, so afternoons are still yours for anything urgent. Come back in two weeks knowing how to work twice as fast. You haven't fallen behind — you've leapt ahead.

Small cohorts of 15 and an in-person setting also mean you get real-time help the moment you're stuck — not a forum post that gets answered three days later.

#### Is there homework or work outside class hours?

Pre-work before the program (4 tasks, about 1–1.5 hours): set up your accounts, have your first expert conversation with Claude, define your problem and what "solved" looks like, and prepare your Materials Kit — a real dataset, documents, and inputs from your own work. During the program, most building happens in class from 9am to 3pm. There's no formal homework, but many builders continue working on their products in the evenings because they're excited about what they're building.

#### What is Demo Day?

Demo Day is the public event that closes every MakerSquare cohort, held on the Friday evening of Week 2. Each builder presents their capstone AI product live to an audience of Austin's tech community — seed-stage investors, operators, and builders. 5-minute live demos with real feedback. It's free to attend and open to the public. The first Demo Day is July 17, 2026. [Learn about Demo Day →](/demo-day)

Logistics

#### Where is MakerSquare located in Austin?

MakerSquare is in Austin, TX. Exact location details are shared with enrolled students. The campus is near downtown Austin, accessible by car and ride-share. Partner housing is available nearby.

#### Is housing included?

No. Housing is not included in tuition. For builders coming from out of town, Austin has a range of short-term rental options near campus. Housing details are shared after enrollment.

#### What do I need to bring?

A laptop (Mac or PC, relatively modern), a willingness to build, and a real problem from your industry you want to solve. Detailed setup instructions and account creation guides are sent in the pre-work packet before the program begins.

#### Can I attend remotely?

No. MakerSquare is an in-person program. The in-person format is not incidental — it's the reason the products get built. A future part-time format (Fridays plus weekends) is planned for professionals who can't take two full weeks away from work, but it will also be in-person in Austin.

After the program

#### What do I walk away with?

A live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — all deployed at public URLs. A Demo Day presentation in front of Austin's tech community. A cohort of builders who become your long-term network. A certificate of completion shareable on LinkedIn. And the practical skills to keep building — the tools, the mental models, and the confidence that comes from having shipped something real.

#### Is there a certificate?

Yes. MakerSquare issues a certificate of completion that is shareable on LinkedIn. More importantly, you leave with a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — deployed — which are a more credible demonstration of skills than any certificate.

#### What's the alumni network like?

All MakerSquare graduates get lifetime access to the alumni Slack, where builders across cohorts share what they're building, swap resources, and find collaborators. The cohort itself — a small cohort who spent 2 weeks in the same room, shipping together — tends to stay tight. Cohort 1 graduates in July 2026.

#### Will this help me get a job in AI?

MakerSquare is not a job placement bootcamp. It's a builder program for professionals who want to use AI in their current work or build something new. That said, demonstrating 3 shipped AI products at Demo Day in front of Austin's tech community has real value for anyone looking to transition into AI-adjacent roles or showcase AI fluency to current or future employers.

#### What if I don't ship all three builds?

That's the guarantee: complete the program and leave with a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — deployed — or receive a full refund. The curriculum and pace are designed so that shipping is the expected outcome, not the exceptional one. Instructors are in the room to make sure everyone ships.

#### Still have questions?

Email us at hello@makersquare.ai — we reply same day. Or just enroll: no interview, confirmed in 24 hrs.

# MakerSquare vs. Wharton, General Assembly & More (2026)

> Honest comparison of MakerSquare vs. Wharton AI ($13,500), UT Austin, General Assembly, Section, and Maven: price, format, and what you ship.

2026 Comparison

## MakerSquare vs. Wharton, UT Austin, General Assembly & Online AI Courses

There are more AI training programs launching every month. This page gives you an honest, specific comparison — price, format, duration, and what you actually walk away with — so you can decide which one is right for you.

**MakerSquare is the only multi-week in-person AI builder program currently available.** Every other multi-week program is online, evenings, or async — lecture decks and video calls, not building. If you want immersive, in-person, and long enough to actually change how you work — there is currently one option.

| | Wharton AI Generative AI for Business | UT Austin AI & ML / Exec Ed | General Assembly AI/ML Part-Time | Section / Maven Live Online Cohorts | GetSmarter University short courses | MakerSquare Austin, TX · In-Person |

Program by Program

### Detailed comparisons

What each program is actually good for — and where MakerSquare is and isn't the right fit.

### MakerSquare vs. Wharton Generative AI for Business

Wharton's Generative AI for Business executive program is one of the most prestigious AI training options available. It runs for 4 consecutive in-person days at approximately $13,500. The audience is senior executives — the content is strategy, governance, and organizational use of AI, delivered at the Wharton level of intellectual rigor.

MakerSquare is $3,999 for 10 full days of in-person instruction. The audience is operators, founders, and domain experts who want to build AI tools themselves — not manage teams who build them. You leave with a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — deployed; Wharton participants leave with frameworks and strategic clarity.

Wharton AI — best for

- C-suite executives setting AI strategy for large organizations

- People who need brand credibility alongside the content

- Governance, ethics, and AI policy discussions

- Those whose budget is not a constraint

MakerSquare — best for

- Operators and founders who want to build, not just strategize

- People who want deployed products by the end, not frameworks

- Anyone who wants 10 days for the price of Wharton's 4

- Non-technical professionals who need no prerequisites

Bottom line: Wharton is the right choice if you're a senior executive who needs strategic AI fluency and institutional credibility. MakerSquare is the right choice if you want to build. At $13,500 for 4 days vs. $3,999 for 10 days, the price-to-hands-on-time ratio heavily favors MakerSquare for anyone whose goal is to leave with working AI tools.

### MakerSquare vs. UT Austin AI Programs

UT Austin offers AI training through multiple channels: McCombs School of Business executive education, continuing education through UT's Professional Education arm, and online programs run in partnership with Great Learning and edX. Prices range from approximately $2,800 for a 9-month online program to $5,000+ for executive-level offerings. Most are delivered online with async content and live virtual sessions.

MakerSquare is also in Austin — physically. Students are in the same city, building in person, and connecting with Austin's operator and tech community. For Austinites or anyone willing to travel to Austin for 2 weeks, the comparison is direct: 9–12 weeks of online coursework at a similar price vs. 2 weeks of in-person immersion that ends with a live Demo Day in front of Austin's tech community.

UT Austin AI — best for

- Students who want UT's institutional brand on their resume

- People who prefer a slower, semester-style pace with flexibility

- Those who cannot take 2 weeks away from work or family

- ML and Python-oriented learners comfortable with technical depth

MakerSquare — best for

- Professionals who want live AI tools, not a certificate

- People who've tried online courses and not finished them

- Non-technical operators who need zero coding prerequisites

- Austinites who want to build and connect locally

Bottom line: UT Austin is a strong choice for technical learners who want academic depth and a recognized credential at their own pace. MakerSquare is the choice for non-technical professionals who want to leave with something deployed. Both are in Austin — only one of them is in Austin with you, in person.

### MakerSquare vs. General Assembly AI/ML Program

General Assembly is one of the most recognized names in tech education. Their AI/ML part-time program runs approximately 12 weeks, Monday and Thursday evenings from 6–9pm, fully online, at around $4,000. It's a structured curriculum with projects and instructor support — a serious program for working professionals who want to upskill without quitting their job.

MakerSquare is the same price and a very different experience. Two weeks, full days, in person. The tradeoff is real: General Assembly fits around your existing life; MakerSquare requires you to step away from it for 2 weeks. What you get for that commitment — real, working AI tools, a public Demo Day, a small cohort of other serious professionals in the same room — is not available in an evening program by design.

General Assembly — best for

- Working professionals who genuinely cannot take 2 weeks off

- People who prefer a structured evening curriculum over immersion

- Those who want the General Assembly brand recognition

- Learners who want a longer runway to absorb material

MakerSquare — best for

- Professionals who can commit 2 weeks and want maximum output

- People who've done evening programs and found them too easy to deprioritize

- Operators who want a live site, an agent, and an automated workflow running in their business immediately

- Those who want a public Demo Day as a proof point

Bottom line: same price, completely different format. General Assembly is right if you need to fit learning around your life. MakerSquare is right if you're willing to step away from your life for 2 weeks to change it. The completion rate and shipped-product outcomes are very different between evening programs and immersive ones — that's the honest trade-off.

### MakerSquare vs. GetSmarter University Short Courses

GetSmarter is not a school. It is a delivery platform owned by 2U that partners with universities — MIT, Oxford, Cambridge, LSE and others — to run their online short courses. So “a GetSmarter course” always means a specific university’s course delivered on GetSmarter’s platform, which is why the name shows up next to institutions that otherwise have nothing to do with each other. Courses run 6 to 12 weeks online, part-time, with weekly modules and real deadlines, and you finish with a certificate from the partner university. Pricing depends entirely on which university: MIT’s 6-week digital business strategy course runs about $2,800, Oxford’s executive leadership programme about $2,711.

The comparison with MakerSquare is unusually clean, because the two are not trying to do the same thing. GetSmarter sells you a university credential earned online around your job. MakerSquare sells you two weeks in a room in Austin and three deployed products. If a hiring manager or a promotion committee needs to see an institution’s name, GetSmarter delivers something we cannot. If you need something running on your own data by month end, a certificate does not do that.

GetSmarter — best for

- A credential with a recognised university name on it

- Learning part-time without taking leave or travelling

- Structured deadlines rather than pure self-paced video

- Anyone outside Austin who wants institutional weight

MakerSquare — best for

- Leaving with deployed products rather than a certificate

- People who want the tools built on their own real work

- Non-technical builders who do not want prerequisites

- Anyone who has finished an online course and still cannot build

Bottom line: pick GetSmarter if the credential is the point — it is the cheaper way to get a university name attached to your AI education, and the deadlines make it more likely you finish than a self-paced course. Pick MakerSquare if what you actually need is a working tool. On the question people search for most, Wharton versus GetSmarter: Wharton is roughly five times the price for four in-person days and an executive-education brand, while GetSmarter is weeks of structured online work for a partner university’s certificate. Neither ends with you having built anything that runs.

### MakerSquare vs. Section, Maven & Live Online AI Courses

Section (formerly Section4) and Maven both offer cohort-based live online AI courses — typically 4–6 weeks, evening or weekend sessions, at $500–$2,000. These are among the better online options: live instruction, peer accountability, and structured cohorts rather than pure self-paced video. Section focuses on business leaders; Maven hosts courses from independent instructors across a range of AI topics.

The advantage over MakerSquare is access and price — you can take these from anywhere and pay significantly less. The trade-off is format: evenings and weekends around a full workweek are chronically deprioritized, the cohort is distributed across time zones, and neither program ends with you having deployed products you built from scratch. They're well-suited for awareness and concepts; MakerSquare is built for people who want to actually ship.

Section / Maven — best for

- Getting AI literacy and a mental model for $500–$2,000

- People who want to test the waters before committing to immersion

- Remote learners who cannot travel to Austin

- Teams that want lightweight async upskilling

MakerSquare — best for

- People ready to move past concepts and actually build

- Professionals who want deployed tools, not completed lessons

- Those who know evening courses don't hold their attention

- Anyone who wants a money-back guarantee tied to real output

Bottom line: Section and Maven are reasonable entry points if you want to understand AI before committing to something intensive. MakerSquare is the right next step when you're ready to stop learning about AI and start building with it. Many MakerSquare-type students have already done an online cohort and found it wasn't enough.

The core difference

### Why no other format produces the same outcomes.

#### Online AI courses have a ~5% completion rate. That's not a motivation problem.

It's a structure problem. When there's no room to show up to, no cohort in the same city, and no consequence for skipping Tuesday's session — most people skip. The content is often fine. The format fails them. In-person with 14 other people who paid real money to be there is a different experience at a structural level.

#### AI skills compound daily. Space them out and you restart every week.

What you learn on Day 4 builds directly on Day 3. Stretch that over 12 weeks with a full job in between and you spend the first 20 minutes of every session catching up instead of pushing forward. Two uninterrupted weeks is the same reason language immersion works and Tuesday evening language class doesn't.

#### The guarantee no other program offers: ship your website, agent, and workflow — or get your money back.

MakerSquare guarantees that every student leaves with a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — deployed live on the internet — not exercises, not wireframes, not certificates. If you complete the 2 weeks and don't have working AI tools deployed, you get a full refund. No other program in this comparison ties their money-back guarantee to a specific shipped outcome. That's how confident we are in the format.

#### Cohort 1 starts July 6, 2026. $3,999. Small cohorts. Open enrollment.

In-person, Austin TX. You leave with a live website, a working AI agent, and an automated workflow — or a full refund. No coding background required.

Schedule An Intro Call

# About MakerSquare | In-Person AI Program in Austin, TX

> MakerSquare closes the gap between people who talk about AI and people who build with it. Founded by Marliis Schneider in Austin, TX.

Our story

## We built MakerSquare because knowing isn't the same as building.

![Marliis Schneider, Founder & CEO of MakerSquare](marliis-headshot.jpg)
Marliis Schneider

Founder & CEO, MakerSquare

[Connect on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/makersquare-ai)
[Featured in Built In “The Biggest Winners of the AI Revolution Aren’t Engineers” Read Marliis’s article →](https://builtin.com/articles/ai-rewards-domain-knowledge)

![Marliis Schneider presenting live demos to a full room at MakerSquare](images/events/demo-night-0984.jpg)
Marliis running our July demo night — Austin, 2026

### The gap that started everything.

Every professional I knew in 2025 was talking about AI. Reading about it, watching demos, sitting in presentations. Most of them were smart, experienced people with real domain knowledge — doctors, lawyers, operators, founders. And almost none of them could actually build anything with it.

That's not a capability problem. It's a format problem. The courses available were online, self-paced, and designed to teach concepts. They were optimized for completion, not for shipping. **The thing that actually moves someone from "I understand AI" to "I built something with AI" is building something, with other builders, under real deadline pressure.**

I'd seen this work before. The original MakerSquare — the coding bootcamp I ran in Austin years ago — proved that immersive, in-person, project-based learning changes what people are capable of. That model produces builders. So the question became: what would that look like for AI, right now, for the professionals who need it most?

### Why we built it the way we did.

The 2-week format is not a compromise. It's the design. Long enough to ship real, working AI tools and build genuine momentum. Short enough that most professionals can take it without putting their life on hold.

The no-coding-required decision was also intentional. **The most valuable AI builders aren't always the ones who know Python — they're the ones who know the problem deeply.** A healthcare administrator who understands a patient intake workflow builds something more useful than an engineer guessing at it. We give domain experts the tools to build what only they can see needs to exist.

Demo Day is the proof of concept for everything. When a builder presents a live AI product in front of Austin's tech community on Day 14 — after arriving with no technical background on Day 1 — that's the argument. That's the product.

### What we believe.

On building

Watching demos doesn't make you a builder. Shipping something does. The program ends when your product is live at a public URL — not when you finish a module.

On domain knowledge

Your industry expertise is not something to work around. It's your edge. A tool built by someone who lived the problem is better than a tool built by someone who read about it.

On format

In-person, immersive learning produces different results than online, self-paced learning. Not always. But when the goal is to ship a product, the room matters.

On honesty

We show you exactly what you'll build, what it costs, and what you'll walk away with before you pay a dollar. No admissions pressure, no income share, no fine print.

Advisory board

### The people who advise us.

![Ravi Parikh](ravi-parikh.jpg)

Ravi Parikh

Co-Founder, MakerSquare · CEO, RoverPass

Ravi and Marliis co-founded the original MakerSquare — one of the most respected coding bootcamps in the country. The program trained thousands of developers before being acquired by Hack Reactor. That track record, and that Austin network, is what the MakerSquare AI program is built on.

After MakerSquare, Ravi founded RoverPass, a booking and management platform for RV parks and campgrounds that he runs as CEO today, and later Parikh Financial. He's spent the last decade building capital-efficient companies from Austin and embedding AI into every team he leads.

He rejoined forces with Marliis to bring MakerSquare back — this time not to train developers, but to turn experienced operators and domain experts into AI builders. The timing is finally right.

![Chris Shonk](chris-shonk.jpg)

Austin-based GP and cofounder of ATX Venture Partners. Serial founder turned investor who's spent his career backing operators through cycles. Believes great companies are built by teams, not term sheets.

Marliis has spent years in the operational trenches. Running teams, building systems, and watching firsthand as AI tools went from novelty to necessity in real businesses.

She built MakerSquare because she kept meeting smart, experienced operators who desperately wanted to use AI but had nowhere to actually learn it in depth. Her background spans operations, business development, and startup ecosystems.

Deeply embedded in Austin's tech and founder community. At MakerSquare, she sets the program vision, owns the curriculum direction, and runs the relationships that make Demo Day matter for graduates.

Ravi Parikh

Ravi and Marliis co-founded the original MakerSquare — one of the most respected coding bootcamps in the country. The program trained thousands of developers before being acquired by Hack Reactor. That track record, and that Austin network, is what the MakerSquare AI program is built on.

After MakerSquare, Ravi founded RoverPass, a booking and management platform for RV parks and campgrounds that he runs as CEO today, and later Parikh Financial. He's spent the last decade building capital-efficient companies from Austin and embedding AI into every team he leads.

He rejoined forces with Marliis to bring MakerSquare back — this time not to train developers, but to turn experienced operators and domain experts into AI builders. The timing is finally right.

What Demo Day is

### Not a graduation ceremony. A product launch.

Most programs end with a certificate ceremony. MakerSquare ends with every builder on stage, in front of a live audience, presenting a product that actually runs. No slideshow. No concept pitch. A working AI product, live, with real data.

#### Live product demos

Every builder gets 5 minutes on stage. The product runs in real time — no pre-recorded footage, no screenshots. Real data, real Claude calls, real output. The audience sees it work or asks why it doesn't.

#### Real audience, real feedback

Seed-stage investors, Austin tech operators, and builders who've shipped their own products. The feedback isn't polite — it's useful. Builders leave knowing exactly what's strong, what to fix, and who in the room wants to talk more.

#### Connections that last

The Austin tech community that shows up to Demo Day is the same network builders tap for their next venture, job, or collaboration. The products you build are your introduction — people remember what they saw running live.

Alumni benefits

### What you get for life after Demo Day.

Graduation isn't the end. MakerSquare alumni stay connected to each other, to the Austin tech community, and to everything being built in future cohorts.

#### Lifetime alumni Slack

Permanent access to the MakerSquare alumni network — builders across every cohort, sharing what they're shipping, answering each other's questions, and finding collaborators.

#### Demo Day access — every cohort

Priority invites to every future Demo Day. Watch what each new cohort builds, stay current on what's possible with AI, and keep showing up in the room where Austin's builders and investors gather.

#### Referral network

When someone asks "who built your AI tool?" — the answer leads back to MakerSquare. Alumni refer each other for consulting work, collaborations, and hiring. The cohort becomes a permanent professional network.

#### Shareable certificate

A certificate of completion shareable directly to LinkedIn. More importantly, you have live, deployed AI tools — a stronger signal than any credential.

Optional · $49/month

Curriculum updates as tools change, monthly live sessions, job board access, and peer review. Cancel anytime. First month free after graduation. [See details →](/immersive)

#### Office hours access

Alumni can drop into future cohort office hours on Saturdays. When you're building something new six months later and hit a wall, the instructors and the room are still available to you.

Outcomes

### What happens when you leave with real, working AI tools.

#### Deploy AI at work

Most alumni return to their jobs and immediately start deploying AI tools to the problems they know best. The 2 weeks of hands-on building gives them the confidence and the vocabulary to execute — not just propose.

#### Launch something new

For founders, the capstone product often becomes the foundation of their company. With a working product, a Demo Day presentation, and a network in the room — many Cohort 1 builders come in with an idea and leave with a prototype live at a URL.

#### Lead AI for their team

Many alumni go back as the person who can actually build — not just supervise a vendor or evaluate a tool. That shift in positioning — from buyer of AI to builder of AI — changes how their colleagues and leadership see them.

#### Stay in the Austin tech network

Demo Day is the introduction, not the end. Alumni maintain lifetime access to the MakerSquare Slack and stay connected to the Austin investor and operator community that showed up to watch them build.

#### Keep building

The alumni Slack is where builders share what they're shipping next, ask technical questions, and find collaborators across cohorts. The skills don't stop at three builds — they compound.

#### Stand out in a crowded market

Everyone is talking about AI. Almost no one outside of engineering can demonstrate live, deployed AI tools. The people who can build are in a different conversation than the people who can't.

The honest comparison

### Why in-person, when every online course is cheaper?

An online course is genuinely the right call if you need one specific skill and you're self-driven — there are good ones, and they cost a tenth of this. Where they fail is where most people actually get stuck: the moment something breaks and there's no one in the room. Our whole model is being in the room — an instructor at your shoulder for two weeks, a cohort building next to you, and your own real work as the material. That's also why we're in Austin and not on Zoom: the room is the product.

<!-- https://www.makersquare.ai/ai-training-vs-consultants -->

# Train Your Team vs. Hire an AI Consultant | MakerSquare

> Should you hire an AI consultant or train your own team? An honest breakdown of when each wins — on ownership, cost, speed, and what

For companies weighing the options

## Hire an AI consultant, or train your own team?

Both are legitimate answers. They just leave your company in very different places when the engagement ends. Here’s the honest version of the comparison — including when we’d tell you to hire the consultant.

Consultant engagement ends ↓

The tool they built
The know-how
The momentum
What they built stays. The ability to change it, fix it, or build the next one leaves with them.

Trained team ↓

First build
Second build
Every build after
The capability lives in your people. Every problem they solve after we leave costs you nothing extra.

### When a consultant is the right call

- • You need one complex, specialized system — and nobody internal will ever need to touch it

- • The problem is deeply technical (custom ML, heavy integrations) rather than workflow automation

- • Your team genuinely has no bandwidth to learn — and you accept paying again for every change

### When training your team wins

- ✓ The opportunities are spread across your business — sales, ops, marketing, admin — not one system

- ✓ Your people know where the waste is better than any outsider ever will

- ✓ You want the capability to compound — every new hire, tool, and problem gets the same treatment

- ✓ You’d rather own the system than rent access to the people who understand it

| | AI consultant | Trained team |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who understands the system | They do | Your people do |
| After the engagement | Changes mean a new invoice | Capability stays and compounds |
| Cost shape | Recurring — per project, forever | One investment, owned outcome |
| Business knowledge | Learned during discovery, then leaves | Already inside — that’s the edge |
| Best for | One deep, specialized system | Opportunities spread across teams |

Seen in the wild

### What a trained business actually looks like.

RoverPass, an Austin reservation company, runs a live AI ops command center tracking hundreds of campgrounds in real time — built inside the business, by people who know the business, on the same stack we teach.

[Read the case study](/case-study-roverpass)

### Talk it through with us.

Tell us what you’re weighing. If a consultant is genuinely your better option, we’ll say so on the call — and if training fits, you’ll get a proposal within 24 hours.

[Talk to Our Training Team](/corporate#contact)

# Case Study: A Sales AE Built His Own AI Prospecting Tool

> Cameron Dowd, a SaaS account executive with no coding background, built an AI tool that researches accounts and drafts outreach into Gmail.

Case study · Sales

## A sales rep built his own AI prospecting tool. No coding background.

Cameron Dowd sells software for a living. In two weeks at MakerSquare, he built and deployed a tool that researches a target account, drafts personalized outreach in his voice, and drops it into his Gmail — ready to review and send.

Built & deployed in 2 weeks · No coding background · Presented at Demo Day, Capital Factory

### The problem every account executive knows

Good outreach is personalized, and personalization takes time. Research the company, find the angle, write the email — do it well and it doesn’t scale, do it fast and it’s generic. That trade-off is the tax on every sales rep’s day, and it’s exactly the kind of work AI is now genuinely good at.

### What Cameron built

You add a target account. An AI agent researches the company — who they are, what’s changed, why they’d care — and drafts outreach tailored to that account, then saves it as a Gmail draft Cameron reviews and sends. Not a generic sequence tool: real research plus a first draft written for each specific account, done for him.

It runs on the stack we teach — Claude for the reasoning and drafting, Exa for live research, Supabase to hold his accounts, and Composio to connect Gmail. Nothing exotic. The hard part isn’t the technology — it’s knowing the sales motion well enough to point it at the right work. Cameron already knew that.

### Why this matters

Cameron didn’t hire a developer or buy another sales tool. He built exactly the tool his workflow needed, because he understands his workflow better than any vendor does. That’s the whole MakerSquare thesis: you already know where your time goes — we give you the skills to build the thing that gives it back.

Common questions

Did Cameron have a coding background?

No. Cameron is a SaaS account executive. MakerSquare is built for non-technical professionals - no coding test, no prior experience required.

What did he build?

An AI prospecting tool: he adds a target account, an AI agent researches the company and drafts personalized outreach, and it saves the message as a Gmail draft ready to review and send.

What was the stack?

Claude (Anthropic) for the drafting and reasoning, Exa for live research, Supabase to store his accounts, and Composio to connect Gmail - the same stack MakerSquare teaches.

How long did it take?

Two weeks, in person in Austin, presented live at Demo Day at Capital Factory.

### Two weeks from now, you could have built yours.

MakerSquare is a 2-week in-person AI builder program in Austin for professionals with no coding background. [See exactly what you’d build →](/curriculum)

# RoverPass: An AI Ops System Inside a Real Business

> How RoverPass, an Austin campground company, runs a live AI ops command center on the same stack MakerSquare teaches corporate teams.

Case study · Operations

## RoverPass runs on an AI operating system. Here’s what that actually looks like.

RoverPass is an Austin company that handles reservations for campgrounds and RV parks across the country. Its ops team doesn’t check dashboards all day — a live AI command center tracks hundreds of campgrounds in real time and surfaces what needs a human.

Full disclosure: RoverPass CEO Ravi Parikh co-founded MakerSquare. This is where we prove what we teach.

### The problem every ops team knows

When your business runs on hundreds of moving parts — properties, bookings, support requests, payments — someone has to watch all of it. The default answer is people staring at dashboards, pulling reports, and finding out about problems after a customer does. That work is necessary. It is also exactly the kind of work AI is now genuinely good at.

### What RoverPass built instead

A live ops command center: one screen where AI tracks activity across hundreds of campgrounds in real time, watches for exceptions, and routes what matters to the person who should see it. Not a chatbot bolted onto the website — an operating layer inside the business. Humans make the calls; the AI does the watching, sorting, and first-drafting that used to eat the team’s day.

It runs on the same stack we teach at MakerSquare — Claude working against the company’s real data and tools through APIs, with automated workflows around it. Nothing exotic. The hard part isn’t the technology; it’s knowing your business well enough to point the technology at the right problems. That knowledge was already inside the company.

### Why this matters for your team

RoverPass didn’t hire an AI consultancy to build this — it was built inside the business, by people who understand the business. That’s the entire MakerSquare thesis: your team already knows where the waste is. Give them the building skills, and the tools they create fit better than anything an outside vendor would ship — and the capability stays in-house after we leave.

What the same pattern looks like on other teams

- ✓ **Sales:** calls recorded, summarized, logged to the CRM; prospect lists that build and enrich themselves

- ✓ **Marketing:** one piece of content becomes a week of channel-ready posts in your brand voice

- ✓ **Finance & admin:** invoices and documents read and extracted to your books’ format automatically

### Want this inside your business?

We train your team to build it themselves — a private 3-day workshop or a custom program, on your tools and your data. Ask us to walk you through the RoverPass build on the call. Weighing an outside consultant instead? [Read the honest comparison →](/ai-training-vs-consultants)

[Talk to Our Training Team](/corporate#contact)

# Case Study: A Job Seeker Built an AI Company-Matcher

> Ted Kilgore, a job seeker with no technical background, built and deployed JobFit — an AI tool that ranks best-fit companies from a resume.

Case study · Career

## A job seeker built an AI tool to find his best-fit companies.

Ted Kilgore was between roles. In two weeks at MakerSquare, he built JobFit: upload your resume and a target role, and get 30 vetted companies ranked by fit — with hiring signals — so the search targets the right doors instead of every door.

Built & deployed in 2 weeks · No coding background · Presented at Demo Day, Capital Factory

### The problem every job seeker knows

The job search is a numbers game with terrible targeting. You spray applications, hear nothing, and have no signal on which companies actually fit your background or are even hiring for real. The effort goes into volume when it should go into aim.

### What Ted built

You give JobFit your resume and a target role. It researches and returns 30 companies ranked by how well they fit — factoring your background and live hiring signals — so Ted could spend his energy on the 30 that mattered instead of the 300 that didn’t.

It runs on the stack we teach — Claude for the matching and reasoning, Exa for live company research, Supabase to store the shortlist, and Composio to connect his tools. The tool is simple; the value is aim. Ted knew what a good-fit company looked like for him — he built something to find them at scale.

### Why this matters

Ted didn’t wait to become technical or pay for another job-search product. He built the exact tool his search needed, because he understood his search better than any generic tool would. That’s the MakerSquare thesis: you already know your problem — we give you the skills to build the solution that fits it.

Common questions

Did Ted have a technical background?

No. Ted was a job seeker in career transition, not a developer. MakerSquare is designed for non-technical professionals.

What did he build?

JobFit: he uploads his resume and a target role, and the tool returns 30 vetted companies ranked by fit, with hiring signals - so his search targets the right companies instead of spraying applications.

What was the stack?

Claude (Anthropic) for the matching and reasoning, Exa for live company research, Supabase to store the target companies, and Composio to connect his tools - the stack MakerSquare teaches.

How long did it take?

Two weeks, in person in Austin, presented live at Demo Day at Capital Factory.

The 2-week program · what's included

### Everything you need to actually build.

- **10 days of live instruction** 9am to 3pm, Mon–Fri for 2 weeks. Hands-on from day one, no lecture-heavy days.

# 10 AI Tools Every Professional Needs in 2026 | MakerSquare

> Not all AI tools are equal. These 10 are the ones that actually change how knowledge workers write, research, build, and automate — ranked by practical impact.

[← Blog](/blog)

AI Tools

## The 10 AI tools every knowledge worker needs in 2026.

Marliis Schneider

July 10, 2026

5 min read

![The 10 AI tools every knowledge worker needs in 2026.](../images/blog/10-ai-tools-every-knowledge-worker-needs-2026-og.webp)

Key takeaways

- The professionals who get the most from AI aren't using more tools — they're using the right ones with genuine skill.

- Writing and research tools (Claude, Perplexity) tend to deliver ROI fastest because they apply to the broadest range of daily work.

- Coding tools like Cursor now enable non-engineers to build functional software — this is new in 2026 and changes who can create AI-powered workflows.

- The bottleneck is rarely access to tools. It's knowing what to build, how to prompt, and when to trust the output.

Most lists of AI tools are really lists of AI products — every tool that exists, organized by category. This one is different. It covers the 10 tools that consistently show up in the workflows of professionals who have materially changed how they work using AI. The criteria: does it save time on work that actually matters, does it have a learning curve short enough to justify the investment, and is it genuinely better than doing the thing manually. These are not the 10 most-talked-about tools. They are the 10 most useful ones.

### Writing and communication: where most professionals start

Claude is the most capable AI for long-form writing, editing, and reasoning through complex problems. Its context window handles full documents, contracts, and research papers without losing thread — which is where most chatbots fall apart. For writing client proposals, synthesizing meeting notes, or drafting anything that requires nuance over length, Claude outperforms alternatives on consistency and judgment.

Notion AI builds directly into the workspace most teams already use. It's not the most powerful standalone AI, but it removes the friction of switching tools — summarizing pages, generating first drafts, and filling in meeting templates from within the documents where the work lives. For teams that live in Notion, it's the fastest path to AI-assisted work.

Grammarly's AI layer has expanded well beyond spell-check. The 2026 version rewrites for tone, restructures arguments, and flags clarity issues with enough specificity to be genuinely useful. For anyone who writes client-facing communications regularly, it's the lowest-effort upgrade available.

### Research and synthesis: the category that saves the most hours

Perplexity is what Google search would be if it actually answered your question instead of linking to 10 pages that might. It pulls from live sources, cites them, and synthesizes an answer. For market research, competitor analysis, or any question that would otherwise require 45 minutes of tab management, it changes the calculation. It is not as good as deep primary research — but it is dramatically better than most people's current research process.

ChatGPT remains the broadest general-purpose tool in the category, particularly with plugins and web access enabled. Its advantage is familiarity and breadth: more people have workflows built around it, more integrations exist for it, and it handles a wider variety of tasks than any more specialized tool. The weakness is consistency — outputs are less reliable for high-stakes work than Claude, and it requires more verification.

### Building and coding: the tools that changed who can create software

Cursor is an AI-powered code editor that enables professionals with no programming background to build functional software. The model is different from a chatbot that helps you code: Cursor integrates into the development environment itself, suggests entire functions, debugs errors in context, and iterates on existing code without requiring the user to understand every line. MakerSquare teaches Cursor as part of the core curriculum because it's the tool that makes the "build something real" part of AI learning accessible to non-engineers. For anyone who has dismissed building with AI because they don't know how to code, Cursor is where to start.

Replit is a browser-based development environment that requires no local setup. For professionals experimenting with their first AI-powered tools, it removes the onboarding barrier entirely — you can go from idea to running prototype in minutes without installing anything. It is less powerful than a full local setup, but that tradeoff makes sense for early experiments and team members who need to test something without IT support.

### Automation: the tools that work while you don't

Zapier AI has evolved from a simple task automator into a platform for building multi-step AI workflows. The 2026 version allows you to chain AI actions across tools — a new email triggers a Claude summary, which posts to Slack, which updates a Notion database — without writing code. For operations and business owners, automating recurring information workflows is where AI delivers some of its most consistent ROI.

Make (formerly Integromat) handles more complex automation logic than Zapier with a visual interface that maps multi-step workflows as a diagram. For teams building anything beyond basic triggers, Make's flexibility makes the investment worthwhile. The learning curve is steeper, but the ceiling is higher.

### The tool that belongs in every professional's workflow

Custom Claude Projects — where you give Claude a persistent set of instructions, documents, and context — are the highest-leverage thing most professionals haven't built yet. A project where Claude has your writing style, your company context, your product details, and your common workflows changes what every other AI interaction looks like. Building one takes two hours. The ROI compounds daily.

The honest caveat: access to all 10 of these tools is cheap compared to knowing how to use them well. The [BCG research tracking AI ROI](https://www.makersquare.ai/blog/how-to-get-roi-from-ai-at-work) found that five or more hours of structured practice separates regular users from people who tried a tool and moved on. The tool list is the easy part. The skill is what matters.

Frequently asked questions

What are the best AI tools for knowledge workers in 2026?

The highest-ROI tools for most professionals are Claude (writing and reasoning), Perplexity (research), Cursor (building AI-powered tools without coding), and Zapier AI (automating workflows). The right stack depends on the work — writing-heavy roles benefit most from Claude and Notion AI; operators and founders get more from Cursor and Zapier.

How do I choose the right AI tools for my job?

Start with where you spend the most time on repetitive cognitive work — writing, research, data synthesis, or communication. Pick one tool that targets that category and spend five or more hours developing real skill with it before adding a second. Breadth of tools without depth of practice produces very little ROI.

Can non-technical professionals use AI coding tools like Cursor?

Yes. Cursor is designed to make software development accessible to people without a programming background. MakerSquare teaches it as part of a core curriculum for operators, founders, and managers — most with zero prior coding experience. The learning curve is real but shorter than most people expect.

Is it worth paying for AI tools or are free versions enough?

For professionals using AI on real work, paid versions of Claude, Perplexity, and Cursor typically pay for themselves within a few weeks. The free tiers are useful for evaluating tools, but they impose rate limits and context restrictions that become friction at the point where the tools start being genuinely useful.
